statement: Prove that a closed subset of a compact topological space is compact.
solution: Let A be closed in compact X. Given an open cover U of A (by sets open in X), the collection U together with X\A is an open cover of X. By compactness extract a finite subcover; discarding X\A leaves finitely many members of U covering A.

statement: Prove that the continuous image of a compact space is compact.
solution: Let f: X->Y be continuous with X compact. Given an open cover of f(X), pull back each set by f to get an open cover of X; take a finite subcover; the images cover f(X).

statement: Prove that in a Hausdorff space every compact subset is closed.
solution: Let K be compact in Hausdorff X and x∉K. For each y∈K choose disjoint opens U_y∋y, V_y∋x. The U_y cover K; take a finite subcover U_{y1..yn}. Then ∩V_{yi} is an open neighborhood of x disjoint from K, so X\K is open.

statement: Prove that a finite union of compact subsets of a space is compact.
solution: Given an open cover of the union, it covers each compact piece; take a finite subcover of each of the finitely many pieces and union them.

statement: Prove that the union of two connected subspaces sharing a common point is connected.
solution: Suppose A∪B (with p∈A∩B) is disconnected by opens U,V. The point p lies in one, say U. Since A is connected and meets U, A⊆U; likewise B⊆U. Then V∩(A∪B)=∅, contradiction.

statement: Prove that the continuous image of a connected space is connected.
solution: If f(X) were disconnected by opens U,V, then f^{-1}(U), f^{-1}(V) would disconnect X, contradicting connectedness of X.

statement: Prove that [0,1] is connected.
solution: Suppose [0,1]=A∪B with A,B nonempty, disjoint, relatively open, 0∈A. Let c=sup{x:[0,x]⊆A}. Openness of A and B at c yields a contradiction whether c∈A or c∈B.

statement: Prove that every metric space is Hausdorff.
solution: For x≠y set r=d(x,y)/2>0. By the triangle inequality B(x,r)∩B(y,r)=∅, giving disjoint open neighborhoods.

statement: Prove that a subspace of a Hausdorff space is Hausdorff.
solution: Distinct points of the subspace are distinct in the whole space; separate by disjoint ambient opens and intersect each with the subspace.

statement: Prove that a function into a space with the indiscrete topology is always continuous, and a function out of a discrete space is always continuous.
solution: Into indiscrete: the only opens are ∅ and the whole space, whose preimages are ∅ and the domain — both open. Out of discrete: every subset of the domain is open, so every preimage is open.

statement: Prove that a continuous real-valued function on a compact space attains its maximum.
solution: The image is compact in R, hence closed and bounded; a nonempty closed bounded subset of R contains its supremum, which is thus attained.

statement: Prove that a closed subset of a complete metric space is complete.
solution: A Cauchy sequence in the closed set F is Cauchy in the complete ambient space, so it converges; the limit lies in F because F is closed.

statement: Prove that the intersection of finitely many open sets is open.
solution: Two open sets: their intersection is open by the topology axioms. Induct to any finite number.

statement: Prove that the closure of a set A equals A union its limit points.
solution: cl(A) is the smallest closed set containing A. Show A∪A' is closed (its complement is open) and contains A, and that any closed set containing A contains A'. Hence cl(A)=A∪A'.

statement: Prove that a compact subset of a metric space is bounded.
solution: Cover K by balls B(x0,n) for n∈N (x0 fixed); by compactness finitely many suffice, so K⊆B(x0,N) for some N, i.e. K is bounded.

statement: Prove that the projection map from a product space onto a factor is continuous.
solution: The preimage of an open set U in the factor is U×(rest), a subbasis element of the product topology, hence open.

statement: Prove that the closure of a connected set is connected.
solution: If cl(A)=U∪V disconnects it, then A (dense in cl(A)) meets both U and V, disconnecting A — contradiction. So one of U,V misses A, but density forces it empty.

statement: Prove that every compact Hausdorff space is normal.
solution: First show compact Hausdorff is regular (separate a point from a closed set using compactness of the closed set). Then upgrade to normal by separating two disjoint closed (hence compact) sets similarly.

statement: Prove that a map is continuous iff the preimage of every closed set is closed.
solution: Preimage commutes with complement: f^{-1}(Y\C)=X\f^{-1}(C). Open-preimage-continuity is thus equivalent to closed-preimage-continuity.

statement: Prove that in a metric space, a set is closed iff it contains the limit of every convergent sequence of its points.
solution: Metric spaces are first countable, so closure = sequential closure. A set is closed iff it equals its closure iff it contains all such limits.
